mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period leads to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of slower wage growth and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of similar trigger events (empirical robustness).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (industrial production) unexpectedly exceeds its prior month by more than 2%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive, reflecting optimism about economic strength.
failure_condition: No significant return advantage over 1000 alternative monthly shocks (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (index of industrial production) of at least 3% over two months indicates supply-side weakness, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in 80% of such events (empirical failure).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive, reflecting expectations of accommodative policy sustaining equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (mean of all months) during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (labor market employment) by more than 50,000 in a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to labor market weakness and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during analogous shocks in other sectors.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels by at least 2% each predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return through dual demand channel amplification.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +2% AND RSAFS > +2% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both proxies increase by similar magnitudes but in opposite directions (counterfactual test).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to supply-side contraction when INDPRO falls by 4% in a month and UNRATE rises above 6% simultaneously predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to deflationary expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -4% AND UNRATE > 6% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in 80% of similar dual-shock events (robustness).
